title: The __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION macro in stm32h7xx.h is wrong
body:
Hello!

stm32h7xx.h line 106.
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_MAIN   (0x01) /*!< [31:24] main version */
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_SUB1   (0x09) /*!< [23:16] sub1 version */
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_SUB2   (0x00) /*!< [15:8]  sub2 version */
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_RC     (0x00) /*!< [7:0]  release candidate */
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION        ((__CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_MAIN     << 24)\
                                      |(__CMSIS_DEVICE_HAL_VERSION_SUB1 << 16)\
                                      |(__CMSIS_DEVICE_HAL_VERSION_SUB2 << 8 )\
                                      |(__CMSIS_DEVICE_HAL_VERSION_RC))

The result of this macro will always be 0

Here is the correct version:
#define __STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION  ((__STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_MAIN << 24)\
                                          |(__STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_SUB1 << 16)\
                                          |(__STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_SUB2 << 8 )\
                                          |(__STM32H7xx_CMSIS_DEVICE_VERSION_RC))

title: null pointer dereference of lwip function ip_reass_free_complete_datagram
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * The board: STM32H7B3I-DK
 * IDE: STM32CubeIDE 1.4.0
 * Projects: stm_udp_echo_server, stm_udp_echo_client, stm_tcp_echo_server, stm_tcp_echo_client

**Describe the bug**
The lwip function ip_reass_free_complete_datagram() is used to free a datagram (struct ip_reassdata) and all its pbufs. It's called by the function ip_reass_tmr() timely or the function ip_reass_remove_oldest_datagram() to clear oldest datagram.

When trying to build _struct ip_reass_helper *iprh_, then function ip_reass_free_complete_datagram() dereference the pointer _ipr->p->payload_ as below. 
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/LwIP/src/core/ipv4/ip4_frag.c#L178. 
However, it doesn't check if _ipr->p_ is a null pointer and there is a chance it could be. This will lead to a null pointer dereference bug.  

**How To Reproduce**
1. Run the demo stm_udp_echo_client which includes lwip.

2. Here is a test case which is a pcap structure package that could be used to reproduce the problem.

[testcase0.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/5550488/testcase0.txt)


**Additional context**
1. To patch it, lwip should check if _ipr->p_ is null firstly.
2. This bug still exists in the latest lwip, we have reported it to lwip too.

title: TIM15 is missing in macro IS_TIM_SLAVE_INSTANCE
body:
**Describe the set-up**
* I wanted to use TIM15 in slave mode on the NUCLEO-H743ZI2 board (featuring the STM32H743ZIT6 rev. V)
* Init code for TIM15 is generated by CubeIDE 1.4.0, the MCU Package for H7 used is version 1.8.0

**Describe the bug**
 *  runs into a failed assertion when it comes to calling the function HAL_TIM_SlaveConfigSynchro. Therein the macro IS_TIM_SLAVE_MODE checks the Timer Instance features the Slave Mode Control Register SMCR
* The actual bug is that TIM15 is missing in the macro hence the assertion will fail.

**How To Reproduce**
To reproduce the bug USE_FULL_ASSERT needs to be defined. Running the following code should yield the aforementioned error:
`TIM_HandleTypeDef htim15;`
`TIM_SlaveConfigTypeDef sSlaveConfig = { 0 };`
`htim15.Instance = TIM15;`
`HAL_TIM_SlaveConfigSynchro(&htim15, &sSlaveConfig);`


**Additional context**
Bug is fixed for me by extending the macro as printed below. The TIM15 is working as I would expect with regards to the Ref Manual.
`/****** TIM Instances : Slave mode available (TIMx_SMCR.TS available )*********/`
`#define IS_TIM_SLAVE_INSTANCE(INSTANCE)   (((INSTANCE) == TIM1)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM2)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM3)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM4)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM5)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM8)   || \`
`                                           ((INSTANCE) == TIM12)  || \`
`					   ((INSTANCE) == TIM15))`

Oddly enough some other header files (only speaking for H7 series) indeed do contain TIM15 in the macro definition (e.g. stm32h730.h). To me it wouldn't be much of a surprise if the same problem exists in even more files accross the STM32 series, assuming the "silicon" for TIM15 is by and large the same.

My code uses:

My code calls  `xQueueReceiveFromISR()` inside the USART1_IRQ. I am observing issue with `xQueueReceiveFromISR()` (which is called with help of `osMessageQueueGet()`)

to:
```
#define portFIRST_USER_INTERRUPT_NUMBER       ( 6 )

```

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/GCC/ARM_CM4F/port.c#L729

to:
`ucCurrentPriority = *(pcInterruptPriorityRegisters + ulCurrentInterrupt);`

To fix the ASSERT issue.

@rxa1031

title: incorrect implementation of pvPortMalloc by the heap_4.c of FreeRTOS
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * Development board: STM32H7B3I-DK and STM32H7B3I-EVAL
 * IDE and version: STMCubeIDE 1.4.0

**Describe the bug**
The function pvPortMalloc() is used to allocate memory for the required size.
The parameter xWantedSize indicates the length of memory required. However, when the required memory block size is zero. The memory pointer variable pvReturn will keep as NULL. If the configuration configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK is enabled, it will recognize the variable xWantedSize valued zero as an error and handle it with the function vApplicationMallocFailedHook() as shown in https://github.com/FreeRTOS/FreeRTOS-Kernel/blob/5fb26de0194b4ebfd09b37128bf9f3ff6d34c1b7/portable/MemMang/heap_4.c#L253 (also https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/beced99ac090fece04d1e0eb6648b8075e156c6c/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/MemMang/heap_4.c#L249)

**How To Reproduce**
1. Import the Domenstration example ClockAndWeather of the board STM32H7B3I-DK.

2. Enable macro configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK. This is default enabled when I try to debug the program.

3. Run the firmware with a default configuration to reproduce and it will loop infinitely.

4. This problem is caused by the incorrect implementation of the function pvPortMalloc() by heap_4.c of FreeRTOS. This bug is already reported to FreeRTOS as shown in https://github.com/FreeRTOS/FreeRTOS-Kernel/issues/204. 


**Additional context**

To patch it, should return NULL or the next available heap address when the parameter xWantedSize is zero.

comments.body:

Thank you for this report. Unfortunately, for this point, we don't treat aspect related to FreeRTOS in our GitHub repositories. As the ``heap_4.c`` file is out of the scope of STMicroelectronics, any modifications concerning this file are not implemented by our technical team. 

Please allow me to close this issue now. Thank you for your contribution. 

With regards,

title: Buffer Overflow due to wrong pdesc->bDescriptorType
body:
**Describe the set-up**
- Software:
	- STM32Cube MCU & MPU Packages
- Version:
	- STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.8.0

	- static void USBH_ParseCfgDesc(USBH_CfgDescTypeDef *cfg_desc, uint8_t *buf, uint16_t length)

- Location:
  - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L420

- Type:
	- Buffer Overflow.

- Result:
	- The system will parse the wrong descriptor.

- Description:
	- The function USBH_ParseCfgDesc() parses the configuration descriptor, interface descriptor, and endpoint descriptor by input data from a USB device. 
    - It tries to parse the endpoint descriptor when the variable pdesc->bDescriptorType is equal to USB_DESC_TYPE_ENDPOINT as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L420. If the variable pdesc->bDescriptorType is not equal to USB_DESC_TYPE_ENDPOINT, the firmware will try to access further memory until reaching the number pif->bNumEndpoints as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L417. If the variable cfg_desc->wTotalLength is also malformed, the firmware will overflow. If not, some endpoint descriptors will be left unset as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L422. And the firmware behaves unpredictably as shown from line 180 to 200 in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Class/MSC/Src/usbh_msc.c.

- Type:
	- Denial-of-Service.

- Result:
	- The system will hang when trying to set a remote wake-up feature.

- Description:
	- The function USBH_ParseCfgDesc() parses the configuration descriptor, interface descriptor, and endpoint descriptor by input data from a USB device. 
    - And it set the variable cfg_desc->bmAttributes by the input data from the USB device. This variable will be used as part of a judgment in the function USBH_Process() as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_core.c#L643. If the hardware doesn’t support this feature, the system will hang due to a FAIL return value by the function USBH_HandleControl(). 




**How To Reproduce**
1. Running MSC_Standalone application on the STM32H7B3I platform

2. Plug a USB disk

3. Use the attached Bug4.txt to replace the USB device packet. [Bug4.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/5381270/Bug4.txt)

**Additional context**
- To patch it, the program should check if the hardware supports a remote wake-up feature.

	- The system could be configured incorrectly with wrong parameters.  

- Description:
	- The function USBH_ParseCfgDesc() parses the configuration descriptor, interface descriptor, and endpoint descriptor by input data from a USB device. 
    - However, it doesn’t check the validity of the variable cfg_desc->wTotalLength compared with the total length of the input buffer as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L395. This will cause the following program including calling to the function USBH_GetNextDesc(), USBH_ParseInterfaceDesc() and USBH_ParseEPDesc() configure the system incorrectly.


**How To Reproduce**
1. Running MSC_Standalone application on the STM32H7B3I platform

2. Plug a USB disk

3. Use the attached Bug2.txt to replace the USB device packet. [Bug2.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/5381225/Bug2.txt)

**Additional context**
- To patch it, the program should check if reach the end of the input buffer when plus cfg_desc->wTotalLength.

title: No validity chekcing on the variable dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize
body:
**Describe the set-up**
- Software:
	- STM32Cube MCU & MPU Packages
- Version:
	- STM32Cube_FW_H7_V1.8.0
- Verification Hardware Platform:
	- STM32H7B3

**Describe the bug**
- Function:
	- static void  USBH_ParseDevDesc(USBH_DevDescTypeDef *dev_desc, uint8_t *buf, uint16_t length)

- Location:
  - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L355

- Type:
	- Denial-of-Service.

- Result:
  - A malformed USB device packet may cause the system to hang when it tries to communicate with the outside world.

- Description:
	- The function USBH_ParseDevDesc() parses the device descriptor by input data from a USB device. 
    - The valid max packet size of the device descriptor should be 8, 16, 32, and 64 as USB specification required. However, the function USBH_ParseDevDesc() doesn’t check the value of dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_ctlreq.c#L355. The variable dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize will be used as the size to construct the control pipe between host and device as shown in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library/Core/Src/usbh_core.c#L828. If bMaxPacketSize is zero, the firmware will get the error status USBH_FAIL in the function USBH_HandleControl() called by the function USBH_CtlReq() when trying to communicate with the outside world by IN and OUT pipe in the future and the host will try to re-enumerate. This process will loop again and again.


**How To Reproduce**
1. Running MSC_Standalone application on the STM32H7B3I platform

2. Plug a USB disk

3. Use the attached Bug1.txt to replace the USB device packet. [Bug1.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/files/5381197/Bug1.txt)

**Additional context**
- To patch it, the program should check if dev_desc->bMaxPacketSize is equal to 8, 16, 32 or 64. At least, it should be greater than zero.

Hi @rxa1031,

Thank for these details. Unfortunately we couldn't reproduce this issue. We used the same code and configuration that you shared and the temperature values returned by both macros are quite similar. The difference is minor, only 1°C. 

However, to answer your question regarding the difference between both macros : 

- **__HAL_ADC_CALC_TEMPERATURE** : The temperature computation within this macro is using temperature sensor calibration values stored in system memory for each device during production. These calibration values are the temperature sensor raw data acquired value at certain temperature calibrated in factory (30°C and 110°C for STM32H7 case) . The formula used for the temperature computation is detailed in the section **"25.4.33 Temperature sensor"** of the [reference manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/dm00314099-stm32h742-stm32h743-753-and-stm32h750-value-line-advanced-arm-based-32-bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf). ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47858836/102211859-8af17180-3ed4-11eb-9261-a215b5e132fa.png)
The calibration is not performed on some device during production, which is not your case since there is calibration values stored in the dedicated memory address. 


- **__HAL_ADC_CALC_TEMPERATURE_TYP_PARAMS** : The temperature computation within this macro is based on the temperature sensor typical values detailed in the [datasheet ](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/stm32h753vi.pdf) within the section **"6.3.23 Temperature sensor characteristics"** and the formula is described at the beginning of the **__LL_ADC_CALC_TEMPERATURE_TYP_PARAMS** macro description.

These two macros give quite similar temperature values, and the difference is minimal. 


I hope this will help you better understand the difference between these 2 macros.

title: Calling SystemClock_Config() results in call to assert_failed() because of missing assignment uwTickPrio = TICK_INT_PRIORITY

Hello @RKOUSTM ,

After a generated code with help of STM32CubeMX (with STM32Cube MCU Package for STM32H7 Series version 1.8.0), which has FreeRTOS enabled and uses CMSIS V2, I _added endless while loops_ to both the `assert_failed()` and the `Error_Handler()` functions.

When debugging the code it is observed that `assert_failed()` triggers when `SystemClock_config()` is called / executes.

It looks like the HAL library got updated to use the variable 'uwTickPrio' in the function HAL_RCC_ClockConfig, instead of what was used in the older library, `TICK_INT_PRIORITY`.

May ST please help me understand the reason why, 'uwTickPrio' is intentionally initialized to an invalid value.

In order to fix the (assert_failed() function called) issue I have added 
```
	uwTickPrio = TICK_INT_PRIORITY;
```
inside function main() body, just before the comment:
```
  /* USER CODE END Init */s
```

The code now works fine.

Please help me with your inputs.

Thanks,
Rajeev

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @rxa1031,

Thank you for this report. We tried to reproduce the issue you described, but we couldn't notice the problem.

According to the following process of initializing the "uwTickPrio" variable to an invalid value, an update of the time base management is proposed to take into account low frequency systems where, at low frequency, a 1 ms systick interrupt does not allow to do anything else than a treated interrupt. 
```
uint32_t uwTickPrio   = (1UL << __NVIC_PRIO_BITS); /* Invalid PRIO */
```
In HAL_InitTick() function, when checking the tick priority, it is better to relay on __NVIC_PRIO_BITS to check the tick priority limit of ticks instead of the initialized number (3 for M0, 15 for M4/M7).

Thank you again for your contribution.

With regards,

Actually, the point you raised has already been raised in another issue #31. We have discussed this internally and we are working on the implementation of a service to enable Reception Timeout interrupt. A fix will be made available in the frame of a future release.

Regarding the second point, indeed, an error has been introduced in the comment which should rather be :
```
 *    b5     Peripheral initialization status
 *        0  : Reset (Peripheral not initialized)
```
```diff
-*        1  : Init done (Peripheral not initialized. HAL UART Init function already called)
+*        1  : Init done (Peripheral initialized. HAL UART Init function already called)
```
The same correction should be applied in the description of **RxState** bitmap.  Thus, `HAL_UART_STATE_TIMEOUT` should be set to **0xA0U** and not to  0x80U since b5=1.

title: Requesting change to HAL_FDCAN_GetProtocolStatus() and FDCAN_COM_XXX macros
body:
Hello,

Please review the function `HAL_FDCAN_GetProtocolStatus()` implementation and the values assigned to macros `FDCAN_COM_STATE_SYNC`, `FDCAN_COM_STATE_IDLE`, `FDCAN_COM_STATE_RX`, and `FDCAN_COM_STATE_TX` (henceforth referred to as FDCAN_COOM_XXX).

Some observations:
1. Within function `HAL_FDCAN_GetProtocolStatus()` body, only the assignment made to `ProtocolStatus->Activity` is not `right shifted`. I understand this implementation is correct based on current values for `FDCAN_COM_XXX`. However, the values do not coincide with the values in datasheet, and without an API document containing this information, coder / user using the API may assume Activity value to be incorrect.

Requests:
1. Could the values assigned to FDCAN_COM_XXX macros be changed so that the valid values are 0 through 3:
```
#define FDCAN_COM_STATE_SYNC ((uint32_t)0x00000000U) /*!< Node is synchronizing on CAN communication */
#define FDCAN_COM_STATE_IDLE ((uint32_t)0x00000001U) /*!< Node is neither receiver nor transmitter   */
#define FDCAN_COM_STATE_RX   ((uint32_t)0x00000002U) /*!< Node is operating as receiver              */
#define FDCAN_COM_STATE_TX   ((uint32_t)0x00000003U) /*!< Node is operating as transmitter           */
```

2. May you please change `ProtocolStatus->Activity = (StatusReg & FDCAN_PSR_ACT)` to `ProtocolStatus->Activity = (StatusReg & FDCAN_PSR_ACT) >> FDCAN_PSR_ACT_Pos` for ease of understanding.

Please share your views.

Thanks,
@rxa1031

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @rxa1031,

Thank you for your contribution.  Indeed, for ``stm32h7xx_hal_fdcan.c`` and  ``stm32h7xx_hal_fdcan.h`` driver code, there is no problem. As noted in the reference manual, the ``Activity`` bites that are used to monitors the module controller area network communication state are defined in the ``FDCAN protocol status register (FDCAN_PSR)`` as follows: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/63848590/95063098-ccf08100-06f5-11eb-8a39-d74e00cd57c4.png)

So, we don't need to shift these bits in the ``stm32h7xx_hal_fdcan.c`` file and the writing to the LSE[2:0] bits has no effect on the bit value. Since the values assigned to ``FDCAN_COM_XXX`` macros in the ``stm32h7xx_hal_fdcan.h`` file are already correctly set based on the following configuration the Bits 4:3 **ACT[1:0]**:
- 00: Synchronizing: node is synchronizing on CAN communication
- 01: Idle: node is neither receiver nor transmitter
- 10: Receiver: node is operating as receiver
- 11: Transmitter: node is operating as transmitter 

Please allow me then to close this thread. Thank you for your comprehension and thank you again for your contribution.

With regards,

title: Issue with chosen MAX value (i.e. 56) of configMAX_PRIORITIES
body:
Hello,

I was reviewing the FreeRTOS code and the `CMSIS_OS2.C` file and the `macro configMAX_PRIORITIES`

I assume the below statement is incorrect and I have a reason for it:

```
/*  CMSIS-RTOSv2 defines 56 levels of priorities. To be able to use them
 *  all and avoid application misbehavior, configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION
 *  must be set to 0 and configMAX_PRIORITIES to 56
 *
 */
```

Even the declarations like below are incorrect:
`#define configMAX_PRIORITIES                     ( 56 )`

**Observation 1:**
The FreeRTOS code version 10.3.1 (and maybe earlier) have a file named `blocktim.c` at location `FreeRTOSv10.3.1\FreeRTOS\Demo\Common\Minimal\blocktim.c`
The file declares the macro:
```
#ifndef bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY
	#define bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY	( configMAX_PRIORITIES - 4 )
#endif
```

I am not sure whether STM32CubeMX is aware of the above file or whether it has a different file in which above macro is created.

**Observation 2:**
File `CMSIS_OS2.C` declares the `enum named osPriority_t`, with the last three enumerated values as:
```
  osPriorityISR           = 56,         ///< Reserved for ISR deferred thread.
  osPriorityError         = -1,         ///< System cannot determine priority or illegal priority.
  osPriorityReserved      = 0x7FFFFFFF  ///< Prevents enum down-size compiler optimization.

```

**Conclusion:**

In order to allow code being ported to other microcontrollers (maybe non ST Microcontrollers) or debugged using MSVC, changes must be made to code.

From observation 1, `I believe all user implementations should only be allowed to use MAXIMUM PRIORITY value which is one less than bktSECONDARY_PRIORITY i.e.  configMAX_PRIORITIES - 5`

From observation 2 and above conclusion, I believe `the value assigned to configMAX_PRIORITIES should be osPriorityISR + 5`


Please share your opinion.

Regards,
@rxa1031

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @rxa1031,

Thank you for this report. Unfortunately, for first point, we don't treat aspect related to FreeRTOS in our GitHub repositories. As the ``blocktim.c`` file is out of the scope of STMicroelectronics what about reporting this point to the [FreeRTOS GitHub](https://github.com/freertos)? Concerning the second point, the ``configMAX_PRIORITIES`` is set to 56 to support the ``osPriority`` in ``CMSIS V2``  (see [this](https://www.keil.com/pack/doc/CMSIS_Dev/RTOS2/html/group__CMSIS__RTOS__ThreadMgmt.html) link).

Please allow me to close this issue now. Thank you for your contribution. 

With regards,

I am trying to test a piece of legacy 16 bit RTXC code by porting it to STM32H7 and FreeRTOS. I found that I need more break points than that currently supported by Keil, so I switched to FreeRTOS 10.3.1 simulator (FreeRTOS\DEMO\Win32-MSVC\WIN32.sln).
I imported the CMSIS_OS.C and CMSIS_OS.H files (that I retrieved from one of the STM32 FreeRTOS examples that is generated by STM32CubeMX) to the FreeRTOS simulator project / code.

After compilation, I am observing the shared concern / _warning_ for `xTaskCreate()`
The third argument is of type _configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE_ which is typedef as below:
	`#define configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE uint16_t`

The _reason for the issue_ is that `thread_def->stacksize` is of type `uint32_t`, which is the right type when passing to `xTaskCreateStatic`, but is not the write type when passing to `xTaskCreate`. Either the two FreeRTOS functions need to update their API argument type (in which case it may be better to update the xTaskCreate argument type) (_For this a request must be raised from your side to FreeRTOS_) or otherwise typecase the variable while passing it to argument 3 of xTaskCreate.

I am UNABLE to use the latest released FreeRTOS version 10.4.0, unless STMicroelectronics immediately upgrade their STM32CubeMX to allow using FreeRTOS version 10.4.0. I have already been asking them to move to FreeRTOS version 10.3.1 for quite a long time now. The biggest issue with Replacing /updating the FreeRTOS files is that the moment someone opens the IOC (project file) in STM32CubeMX and regenerates the code, the FreeRTOS 10.4.0 files will again get overwritten with FreeRTOS 10.2.1 files.

Regards,
@rxa1031

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @Paullake85, 

According to our development team, the configuration you have used
```
#define DATA_AREA USE_INTERNAL_SRAM
#define CODE_AREA USE_INTERNAL_SRAM
```
is not supported in the application. The available configurations are detailed in the readme file in the [Table 1. IAP implementation on STM32H7B3I-DISCO](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Projects/STM32H7B3I-DK/Applications/ExtMem_CodeExecution/ExtMem_Boot/readme.txt#L123).

In order to be able to run the application with the chosen configuration ,which is the use of the internal SRAM for both Code and Data area,  you have to perform some modification as following:

1. Identify different address for each zone for example :

```
#define INTERNAL_SRAM1  0x24010000UL  for data  
#define INTERNAL_SRAM   0x24000000UL  for code   
```


2.  Insert the APPLICATION_ADDRESS to preprocessor defines and set an appropriate value 

`APPLICATION_ADDRESS=0x24000000U`

3. Copy the project.bin to OSPI memory and follow the same steps as BOOTROM example

Finally, to answer your question, the `BINARY_SIZE` correspond to the size of the generated project.bin of the application to be executed.

Best regards,

title: FreeRTOS-MPU fails to run if its privileged RAM is in a cacheable memory region
body:
## The setup

- Hardware: Nucleo-H743ZI2
- IDE: IAR for Arm v8.32.1

## The bug

FreeRTOS-MPU faults during initialization because of a cache coherency issue with `pxCurrentTCB`; allocated in the Privileged RAM region.

The SDK example only works because the Privileged RAM section is allocated in DTCM, a non-cacheable memory region.

To solve it, that memory region should be set as non-cacheable in the MPU. That way it can be allocated in cacheable memory regions.

In more technical detail:

- FreeRTOS-MPU allocates `pxCurrentTCB` in the privileged RAM section.
- During `xPortStartScheduler`, the privileged RAM section is allocated in the MPU as cacheable
- As a result, if the DCache is enabled, pxCurrentTCB will be cached.
- Cache coherency is lost during the initialization of the RTOS' scheduler, the assembly routine `vPortRestoreContextOfFirstTask` attempts to access a Reserved memory region, and results in a hard fault

## How To Reproduce

0. Grab the FreeRTOS-MPU sample application from the SDK
1. Fix the FreeRTOS-MPU bug described in issue #38 so the MPU is enabled
2. Update the linker script and `main.c` to allocate the Privileged Data section into AXI ram instead of DTCM
3. If you're using different hardware than me, make sure the DCache is enabled and has access to the AXI SRAM region you set up in the previous step
4. Try to run the application, and you should get a crash right away. Or perhaps some other serious misbehavior, depending on which incorrect values are loaded into your registers from `vPortRestoreContextOfFirstTask`

## Additional context

For a minimum viable fix, a couple of things need to be updated in each FreeRTOS-MPU port affected by this bug:

1. `portmacro.h` needs to support "normal, shareable, non-cacheable" configurations of MPU->RASR registers. That's `TEX=001 S=1 B=0 C=0` according to [the docs](https://developer.arm.com/docs/dui0646/a/cortex-m7-peripherals/optional-memory-protection-unit/mpu-access-permission-attributes#BIHHEDAE):
    `#define portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ( 0x0cUL << 16UL )`
2. Privileged RAM needs to be configured using that `portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE` **instead of** `portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE`.
    - In `prvSetupMPU`:
    ```
         portMPU_REGION_ATTRIBUTE_REG =  ( portMPU_REGION_PRIVILEGED_READ_WRITE ) |
    #if 0 /* Original code */
                                         ( portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE ) |
    #else /* fix */
                                         ( portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ) |
    #endif
                                         prvGetMPURegionSizeSetting( ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_end__ - ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_start__ ) |
                                         ( portMPU_REGION_ENABLE );
    ```
    - In `vPortStoreTaskMPUSettings`:
    ```
        xMPUSettings->xRegion[ 1 ].ulRegionAttribute =
                ( portMPU_REGION_PRIVILEGED_READ_WRITE ) |
    #if 0 /* Original code */
                ( portMPU_REGION_CACHEABLE_BUFFERABLE ) |
    #else /* fix */
                ( portMPU_REGION_SHAREABLE_NON_CACHEABLE ) |
    #endif
                prvGetMPURegionSizeSetting( ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_end__ - ( uint32_t ) __privileged_data_start__ ) |
                ( portMPU_REGION_ENABLE );
    ```
Alternatively, memory barriers could be used to ensure the coherency of pxCurrentTCB, but I was not successful in my attempts, and I'm not sure if other FreeRTOS variables would still be affected in more insidious ways.

## More context

The fix described earlier got me past this problem, but I'm still running into other crashes shortly after. These may or may not have related causes; I'm still investigating.

If you uncover any other issues while fixing this one, a heads-up would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,
JC

title: FreeRTOS-MPU does not use the MPU on M7 cores
body:
I've reported this bug through your [forums](https://community.st.com/s/question/0D53W000003yAyDSAU/unable-to-set-up-noncacheable-mpu-regions-for-lwipethernet-when-using-freertosmpu-on-stm32h743zi) and the support portal. Feel free to close the issue if it's already been escalated/solved internally.

- Hardware: Nucleo-H743ZI2
- IDE: IAR for Arm v8.32.1

All M7 cores are affected, regardless of the compiler used.

## The bug

The FreeRTOS-MPU ports provided for M7 cores (ARM_CM4_MPU and ARM_CM7_MPU), and possibly others, do not actually use the MPU.

From `ARM_CM4_MPU/port.c`:

```
    #define portEXPECTED_MPU_TYPE_VALUE             ( 8UL << 8UL ) /* 8 regions, unified. */
```

M7 cores support 16 MPU regions, so that MPU->TYPE value is incorrect. As a result, the port silently fails to initialize the memory protection unit.

The fix:

```
    #if defined(CORE_CM4)
        #define portEXPECTED_MPU_TYPE_VALUE         ( 8UL << 8UL ) /* 8 regions, unified. */
    #else
        #define portEXPECTED_MPU_TYPE_VALUE         ( 16UL << 8UL ) /* 16 regions, unified. */
    #endif /* defined(CORE_CM4) */
```

That `#if defined(CORE_CM4)` is in line with the implementation at stm32h7xx_hal_cortex.h

## How to reproduce

1. Run the FreeRTOS-MPU example from the SDK on an M7 MCU
2. Use your debugger of choice to check the MPU->CTRL register. It will show that the MPU is disabled
3. Implement the fix mentioned above, and MPU->CTRL will show the MPU is now enabled, as expected

## After this fix

After fixing this bug, a different one came up. When I try to use FreeRTOS-MPU and the MPU HAL on the same app, I run into a crash within the assembly routine `vPortRestoreContextOfFirstTask` of the ARM_CM4_MPU port. I'm still debugging that new one, and awaiting response from your support guys.

If you'd like any more info, let me know.

  * From the startup tab, load **both** binaries into the flash memory.
  * Screenshots:
    * Startup tab.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84530219-ac319500-acda-11ea-945d-47da3edd39f5.png)
    * Debugger tab.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84528610-ed747580-acd7-11ea-83c1-f147cc8e7bf1.png)
* Create a **second** debug configuration for the **CM4** sub-project using the **ST-Link GDB Server** probe.
  * From the startup tab, **do not** load CM4-related binary into the flash memory.
  * From the debugger tab, perform also an **Autostart** of the server, but pay **attention** to:
    * Increment the GDB port number (+2 for example).
    * Set the reset type to **none**.
  * Screenshots:
    * Startup tab.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84529418-56a8b880-acd9-11ea-819c-2691b0df978d.png)
    * Debugger tab.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84529994-4c3aee80-acda-11ea-80b9-f9e0555990c0.png)
* Run the CM7 core.
  * Code execution should break at the level of the first instruction, **i.e.** the modified while loop.
* Run the CM4 core.
  * Code execution should break at the level of the first instruction, **i.e.** `__HAL_RCC_HSEM_CLK_ENABLE();`.
  * Set a break point on the `HAL_Init();` instruction. This will serve later.
  * So far, this is how your Cube IDE window should look like.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84547422-6df89d80-acfb-11ea-80e2-6fccf09427ca.png)
* Resume the CM4 code execution.
  * It shall enter the sleep mode.
  * On the CM4 sub-project window, you should read that execution broke at address **0xa05f0000**.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84547857-40f8ba80-acfc-11ea-896b-bba6985f61d7.png)
* Resume the CM7 code execution.
  * The CM7 core will wake the CM4.
  * The GDB client is not aware that the CM4 core woke up. Nothing particular will be displayed on the CM4 sub-project window.
* Now, simply click on the "suspend/resume" button of the CM4 sub-project.
  * The window should display the C code again.
  * Code execution should halt at the level of the `HAL_Init();` instruction (thanks to the beak point we set earlier).
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46019491/84548318-3ee32b80-acfd-11ea-8f74-778a56ebe11e.png)
* Now you can debug execution on both cores as you wish.

I hope this tutorial will finally help you enjoy this dual core example. Please do not hesitate in case you still face some issue.

With regards,

title: CubeMX: 0-pointer access in generated code if TIM6 is used for HAL tick and DAC is enabled
body:
Hi!

I don't know where to report CubeMX bugs, so I leave it here. It might also be considered a HAL problem.

I noticed this behavior after enabling a MPU region to catch 0-pointer accesses.

If TIM6 is used as the HAL Timebase **and** the DAC is enabled, there may be a 0-Pointer access in HAL_DAC_IRQHandler (called by TIM6_DAC_IRQHandler), **if** a tick IRQ happens before MX_DAC1_Init() is called.

The same bug likely exists in all other HAL and CubeMX versions.

Simple workaround: Use another timer, that has a non-shared IRQ handler.

best regards,
Thomas

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @thomask77 ,

Thank you for this report. We tried to reproduce the issue you described, but we couldn't notice the problem. May I ask you if you were able to reproduce it, and if so what is the procedure followed to get it ?

According to a first analysis, we noticed that CubeMx initializes by default the DAC1 before initializing the TIMx instances. Thus, MX_DAC1_Init() is always called before MX_TIM6_Init(). Therefore, no TIM interruption is generated before DAC initialization.

Moreover, the code generated by CubeMx remains just an initialization, so, no Timbase interruption is enabled until the user implicitly activates them either by calling the interrupt mode APIs (such as `HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT()` ) or by activating the update interruption ( calling `__HAL_TIM_ENABLE_IT(htim, TIM_IT_UPDATE)` or directly enabling `TIM_DIER_UIE` bit).
 
Take care and stay safe.

With regards

comments.author: thomask77
comments.body:
Yes, that's the problem - `HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT()` is called!

The call chain is:
- `main()`
- `HAL_Init()`:
  - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal.c#L134
- `HAL_InitTick()` (weak function, overridden by CubxMX with a file derived from a template contained in this repository):
  - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_timebase_tim_template.c#L58
- `HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT()`:
  - https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_timebase_tim_template.c#L114-L121

This happens before `HAL_DAC_Init()` is called.

Null pointer access is then triggered here:

```c
void TIM6_DAC_IRQHandler(void)
{
  /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */

  /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 0 */
  HAL_DAC_IRQHandler(&hdac1);
  HAL_TIM_IRQHandler(&htim6);
  /* USER CODE BEGIN TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */

  /* USER CODE END TIM6_DAC_IRQn 1 */
}
```

`HAL_DAC_IRQHandler` will use the uninitilized `Instance` pointer.


Steps to reproduce:
* Start CubeMX 5.6.0
* Select NUCELO-H743ZI in Board Selector
* Init all peripherals to default mode -> Yes (doesn't matter)
* System Core -> SYS -> Timebase Source: TIM6
* Analog -> DAC1, OUT1 mode: Connected to external pin only

Generate code.

title: USART Receive timeout interrupt not enabled.
body:
**Describe the set-up**
Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32H743 and external FLASH and external SDRAM.
IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1
 
**Additional context**
Setting up the UART receive timeout involves calling these functions:
`HAL_UART_ReceiverTimeout_Config(mHuart, mBitsPerCharacter);
HAL_UART_EnableReceiverTimeout(mHuart);`

However, that does not enable the receive timeout **interrupt**.  The timeout detection is enabled, but not the interrupt.  The following line should be added to the 'enable' routine, or placed in a separate call:

`SET_BIT(mHuart->Instance->CR1, USART_CR1_RTOIE);`

Also, after the receive completes, the interrupt should be disabled.

`CLEAR_BIT(mHuart->Instance->CR1, USART_CR1_RTOIE);`

title: Wrong timer identifiers on some HRTIM functions doc
body:
The HRTIM header contains the following definitions as timer identifiers
```c
/** @defgroup HRTIM_Timer_identifier HRTIM Timer identifier
  * @{
  * @brief Constants defining timer identifiers
  */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_MASTER  (HRTIM_MCR_MCEN)   /*!< Master identifier  */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_TIMER_A (HRTIM_MCR_TACEN)  /*!< Timer A identifier */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_TIMER_B (HRTIM_MCR_TBCEN)  /*!< Timer B identifier */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_TIMER_C (HRTIM_MCR_TCCEN)  /*!< Timer C identifier */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_TIMER_D (HRTIM_MCR_TDCEN)  /*!< Timer D identifier */
#define HRTIM_TIMERID_TIMER_E (HRTIM_MCR_TECEN)  /*!< Timer E identifier */
```

Some HRTIM functions (e.g. HAL_HRTIM_WaveformCountStop) incorrectly have those definitions documented as
```c
  * @param  Timers Timer counter(s) to stop
  *                   This parameter can be any combination of the following values:
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_MASTER
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_A
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_B
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_C
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_D
  *                   @arg HRTIM_TIMERID_E
```

As far as I can tell those don't exist, not even as legacy definitions.

title: HAL_RTC_Init() looses time
body:
**Describe the set-up**
I'm using a STM32H743 on a custom board with 32768 Hz LSE crystal and battery-backed up RTC.

**Describe the bug**
Every time `HAL_RTC_Init()` is called, the RTC looses some sub-seconds.

`HAL_RTC_Init` should check if the RTC is already initializied (year != 0) and/or matches the desired configuration, and skip unnecessary stopping of the clock. According to the data sheet 45.3.8, the library should also check the `INITS` flag in the RTC_ISR register.

This is big a problem, because CubeMX5 will emit code that calls `HAL_RTC_Init` on each reset, without checking if it's already initialized. On each reset, you will loose up to 1s.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Read time with `HAL_RTC_GetTime` &`HAL_RTC_GetDate` and print to console
2. Call `HAL_RTC_Init`
3. Repeat

While doing this, the clock will gradually loose seconds.

title: STM32CubeMX code generator is calling ethernetif_input instead of ethernet_link_thread.
body:
**Describe the set-up**
* Hardware:  Proprietary hardware containing STM32H743 and external FLASH and external SDRAM.
* IDE:  VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1
* FreeRTOS: V10.1.2
* CMSIS: V2.0
* Package:  STM32Cube FW_H7 V1.6.0

**Describe the bug**
When LWIP_NETIF_LINK_CALLBACK is enable in the STM32CubeMX LWIP middleware, it generates the following code from the FW_H7 V1.6.0 package:

```
/* Set the link callback function, this function is called on change of link status*/
  netif_set_link_callback(&gnetif, ethernet_link_status_updated);
 
  /* Create the Ethernet link handler thread */
  memset(&attributes, 0x0, sizeof(osThreadAttr_t));
  attributes.name = "EthLink";
  attributes.stack_size = INTERFACE_THREAD_STACK_SIZE;
  attributes.priority = osPriorityRealtime;
  osThreadNew(ethernetif_input, &gnetif, &attributes);

```
In the last line, it is starting a thread with an entry function of ethernetif_input.  However, that function has nothing to do with the ethernet link status.  Previous versions of this package used an entry function for the thread called ethernet_link_thread.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project
Proprietary application with Ethernet port and LWIP as the TCP/IP stack.

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...)
The **_MX_LWIP_Init()_** function in the file **_lwip.c_**.

3. The use case that generates the problem
See (4)

4. How we can reproduce the problem
Create an STM32CubeMX project that uses the FW_H7 V1.6.0 package and includes LWIP middleware with the LWIP_NETIF_LINK_CALLBACK option enabled. The code that initiates the thread that monitors the Ethernet link uses the wrong start function.


**Additional context**
This code in MX_LWIP_Init():
`osThreadNew(ethernetif_input, &gnetif, &attributes);`
should be changed to:
`osThreadNew(ethernet_link_thread, &gnetif, &attributes);`

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

title: SDMMC: Hard-coded clock dividers only work for 200MHz MMCCLK
body:
For MMC and SD-Card operation, the clock dividers are hard-coded and work for 200 MHz `sdmmc_clk` _only_:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/3d3ffbe6e15fc7e4d8a4d275e9fb3a334e31c8a3/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_ll_sdmmc.h#L697-L704

CubeMX5 allows to configure the SDMMC peripheral with up to 480 MHz, so the clocks will be much to fast (e.g. 960 kHz during init instead of 400 kHz).

-> The dividers should be re-calculated according to the peripheral clock in  `stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c` and `stm32h7xx_hal_mmc.c`.

(`stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c` already uses `HAL_RCCEx_GetPeriphCLKFreq(RCC_PERIPHCLK_SDMMC)` to calculate some delays. This must also be done for the divisors).

comments.body:

The issue you pointed out has been communicated to our development teams. It will be investigated soon. We will be back to you as soon as we get an answer. Thank you for your patience.

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi thomask77,

Our development team  has confirmed the issue you pointed out and here is their reply :

The clock divider is configured through the init structure to allow the user setting the desired clock frequency. So, the user could use either the define provided in the .h file or define his own dividers.
But since the high speed and ultra-high speed features have been implemented, these define are also used in the driver. Then, as indicated in the issue, to have the appropriate clock frequency when not running at max frequency, it should be necessary to calculate the correct divider and not use directly the define.

Since the issue is confirmed, a fix will be implemented and made available in future release. Thank you once again for pointing out the issue and for your active contribution.

With regards,

title: __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET() sometime causes microprocessor to reset
body:
**Setup**
Hardware: Proprietary hardware containing STM32H743 and external FLASH and external SDRAM.
IDE: VisualGDB with GCC 9.2.1

**Bug Description**
When the HAL_DeInit() function calls the __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET() function the microprocessor sometimes resets.

    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET()          (RCC->AHB3RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project
A small FLASH programmer is running in internal RAM (DTCMRAM @ 0x20000000).  After it programs the external flash it unloads itself and calls HAL_DeInit() which calls __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET().  At this point the microprocessor resets.

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...)
The __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET() resides in stm32h7xx_hal_rcc.h

3. The use case that generates the problem
Calling the HAL_DeInit() when the program prepares to unload itself.

4. How we can reproduce the problem
I don't know all conditions which makes the function fail.  I suspect it has something to do with calling the function from internal RAM.  I don't think you need to reproduce the problem.  It is clearly a bug (see below) which should be rectified.


**Additional context**
The code writes all 1's to the AHB3RSTR register.  However, the STM32H7 reference manual says the reserved bits in that register must remain at the reset value (i.e. 0's)

This code:

    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET()          (RCC->AHB3RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)

should be replaced by:

    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB3_RESET_ALL               (RCC_AHB3RSTR_MDMARST |       \
                                                    RCC_AHB3RSTR_DMA2DRST |      \
                                                    RCC_AHB3RSTR_JPGDECRST |     \
                                                    RCC_AHB3RSTR_FMCRST |        \
                                                    RCC_AHB3RSTR_QSPIRST |       \
                                                    RCC_AHB3RSTR_SDMMC1RST)

    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB3_FORCE_RESET()          (RCC->AHB3RSTR = __HAL_RCC_AHB3_RESET_ALL)    

**Screenshots**
None

comments.author: david-oz00
comments.body:
I've noticed similar functions incorrectly write all 1's to the registers.  E.g

    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB1_FORCE_RESET()             (RCC->AHB1RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_AHB2_FORCE_RESET()           (RCC->AHB2RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_APB3_FORCE_RESET()         (RCC->APB3RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_APB1L_FORCE_RESET()        (RCC->APB1LRSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_APB1H_FORCE_RESET()        (RCC->APB1HRSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_APB2_FORCE_RESET()         (RCC->APB2RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)
    #define __HAL_RCC_APB4_FORCE_RESET()           (RCC->APB4RSTR = 0xFFFFFFFFU)

I haven't seen any detrimental affects from these functions, unlike the one described in the initial report.  However, technically the HAL should not be writing 1's to the reserved bits of these registers.

Hi Jiří,

I asked our development teams for an explanation about this gap between the firmware's and the HAL's versions, particularly as the HAL's precedes the firmware's.

This gap started from the STM32CubeH7 **v1.4.0** published on the 5th of April 2019. In the frame of this publication, CMSIS Device and HAL components were already versioned v1.5.0 both.

Actually, at some point in the past, our development teams have been requested to deliver a major release of CMSIS Device and HAL components **outside the frame of** a firmware package. This has been done on the 30th of November 2018 when version **v1.4.0** of both components has been released.

To summarize, we have:
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.3.0 --> FW v1.3.0
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.4.0 (released as **standalone** components)
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.5.0 --> FW v1.4.0
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.6.0 --> FW v1.5.0
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.7.0 --> FW v1.6.0
* CMSIS D + HAL v1.8.0 --> FW v1.7.0

Below are links to the different release notes in case you would like to have an overview of the different publication dates:
* Release note of the STM32CubeH7 FW package ([link](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Release_Notes.html))
* Release note of the H7 CMSIS Device component ([link](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32H7xx/Release_Notes.html))
* Release note of the H7 HAL driver component ([link](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/master/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Release_Notes.html))

I hope this answers your question and excuse the delayed reply.

With regards,

**PS:** You may notice that in the firmware's release note, version 1.7.0 of the firmware is still reported to integrate version v1.7.0 of both CMSIS Device and HAL components. This is simply a typo that should be corrected soon hopefully.

title: Regression in QSPI vs. v1.3.0
body:
Hi!

**Describe the set-up**

We are using an STM32H743XIH6 (Rev. V) @ 480 MHz, on a custom board with a W25Q128JVEIQ flash in Quad-SPI mode. Our Toolchain is gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2019-q4-major.

**Describe the bug**

We're using the HAL_QSPI_Transmit_DMA function.

When using CubeMX libraries v1.3.0, we could run QSPI with 120 MHz clock (Clock Prescaler 1).

After an upgrade to CubeMX libraries v1.5.0, we had to set the prescaler to 8, or even 16 to achieve stable operation, otherwise, HAL_QSPI_Transmit_DMA would fail. 

We can send you the CubeMX file if required.

**Additional context**

I haven't looked into the bug in detail yet, but I could narrow it down to this single change:

v1.5.0, **bad**:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/e261d820b398846a94f22f4aeb32d86c29546efb/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32h7xx_hal_qspi.c#L1333-L1334

```c
      __HAL_QSPI_ENABLE_IT(hqspi, QSPI_IT_TE);
```

After reverting the change, we can run with 120 MHz again.

What was the reason for the change in 1.5.0?

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi Pavel,

I had a look to the ETH_DMADescTypeDef structure type and I think I understand better your point. Would you confirm please before I loop back with our development teams? Thanks.

Below is the definition of the ETH_DMADescTypeDef structre type:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.h#L57-L65

Now, `sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)` would return 24 (6 members x 4 bytes per member).

And here is the point:
* On the one hand, **removing** the `sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)` from the expression would not yield the correct result, as you are saying (resulting address **less than** the targeted one).
* On the other hand, **leaving** the `sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)` **as it is** would not yield the correct result neither (resulting address **greater than** the targeted one).

Rules of pointer arithmetic require rather the following:
* `sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef) / sizeof(uint32_t)`

Correct implementation would then be:
```diff
-WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc + (((uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1))*sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)))));
+WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc) + (((uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1)) * (uint32_t)(sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef) / sizeof(uint32_t)))));
```

With regards,

comments.body:
Ali, sorry for delay. So now there are two "correct" variants. (I assume that red line with - is wrong and green line with + is proposed correction).

I'm confused.... where is pointer arithmetic in `(uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc)` ? If it were `(uint32_t*)(heth->Init.RxDesc)` then maybe... Lets' ask help from the ethernet experts on the forum.

Regards,
Pavel

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi Pavel,

Pointer arithmetic arrives on the scene because structure member `RxDesc` is actually a **pointer** to the first DMA Rx descriptor.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/blob/79196b09acfb720589f58e93ccf956401b18a191/Drivers/STM32H7xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32h7xx_hal_eth.h#L378
Hence, as `RxDesc` points on a `ETH_DMADescTypeDef` structure, expression `(uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc + (uint32_t)1)`, for instance, will be automatically reevaluated `@firstRxDesc + sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)`.

To conclude, first fix suggestion is the correct one as confirmed by @kele14x.
```diff
-WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc + (((uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1))*sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)))));
+WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc) + ((uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1))));
```
The above expression (in green) will be automatically reevaluated `@firstRxDesc + (ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1) * sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)`.

I hope this makes things clearer. Please do not hesitate if you still have questions about the suggested fix.

With regards,

comments.author: pavel-a
comments.body:
Ali, @kele14x, with all respect it seems there's some misunderstanding.
I put a little example here to explain: [rextester.com/LRKA74918](https://rextester.com/LRKA74918)
As soon as you cast a pointer to a number `(uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc)`, it becomes a number and pointer stuff no longer applies to it.

However, as @alister[ commented on the forum](https://community.st.com/s/question/0D53W000003vOM1SAM/stm32h7-ethernet-please-help-to-review-rx-descriptor-init-fix), it looks like there are multiple variants of setting this register, depending on the overall design of the driver. If the person who proposed the correction will provide also a thorough fix of the ETH driver, he/she likely knows better. If such fix won't be provided, this issue alone is not important.

Regards,
Pavel A.

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi Pavel,

I confirm there is a misunderstanding and a **typo** (from my side) too. In the expression I reported of the suggested fix, **parenthesis** are not correctly placed. With such an expression, pointer arithmetic applies no more. You are absolutely right about it.

The fix would rather be:
```diff
-WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc + (((uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1))*sizeof(ETH_DMADescTypeDef)))));
+WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, ((uint32_t)(heth->Init.RxDesc + (uint32_t)(ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1))));
```

I hope you agree on what is written here. I do apologize for the confusion caused.

With regards,

comments.author: pavel-a
comments.body:
Ali, no problem, thanks for checking. The bigger question now is, how about a deeper revision of the eth driver? When this could be expected?
- P.

comments.author: tushartp
pavel-a
comments.body: @tushartp You're welcome to ask this in the [forum](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BSqSWAW/stm32-mcus).

comments.author: thomask77
comments.body:
To make the code's intention clearer, I would suggest

```c
WRITE_REG(heth->Instance->DMACRDTPR, (uint32_t)(&heth->Init.RxDesc[ETH_RX_DESC_CNT - 1]));
```

Much clearer, and doesn't require knowledge of pointer arithmetic rules.

comments.body:
Hi Liarokapisv,

Here is what the reply of our development teams:
- The I2S full duplex was mentioned as a missed feature in the release notes of the v1.4.0 (***Known Limitations*** section).
- The I2S full duplex feature is not available in the v1.5.0 neither. The files stm32h7xx_hal_i2s_ex.c/.h are protected with a compilation define `#if defined (SPI_I2S_FULLDUPLEX_SUPPORT)`.
- This `SPI_I2S_FULLDUPLEX_SUPPORT` define is **no set by default**. This is to avoid compiling the full duplex feature implemented in these files but not yet ready to be used.

You have probably activated it (and you were right as we provided this feature within the driver). Hence,  you got these errors. We do apologize for this "ambiguity".

This issue will be fixed in two steps:
1. In the next release (v1.6.0), we will remove the stm32h7xx_hal_i2s_ex.c/.h from the package.
2. Once the full duplex correctly implemented, we will put these files back into the package to make this feature available to use.

Thank you once more for having tackled this point.

With regards,

title: SDMMC_BASE is undefined
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc
 * `#include <stm32h7xx.h>`

**Describe the bug**

This line is wrong, since there is no `SDMMC` peripheral on the device.
```c
#define SDMMC               ((SDMMC_TypeDef *) SDMMC_BASE)
```

The correct peripherals are called `SDMMC1` and `SDMMC2` and they are correctly defined.

**How To Reproduce**

Try to call `SDMMC` in your code, which will fail since `SDMMC_BASE` is undefined.

**Additional context**

```diff
-#define SDMMC               ((SDMMC_TypeDef *) SDMMC_BASE)
```
[Full patch](https://github.com/modm-io/cmsis-header-stm32/blob/master/patches/h7.patch)

Also note that there is a use of a *signed* 32-bit integer in the `ETH_TypeDef` struct (around line 762):
```diff
   uint32_t      RESERVED15[14];
   __IO uint32_t MMCTSCGPR;
   __IO uint32_t MMCTMCGPR;
-  int32_t       RESERVED16[5];
+  uint32_t      RESERVED16[5];
   __IO uint32_t MMCTPCGR;
   uint32_t      RESERVED17[10];
   __IO uint32_t MMCRCRCEPR;
```

title: HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef is undefined
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc
 * `#include <stm32h7xx.h>`

**Describe the bug**

`HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef` is undefined. After cross referencing this with the RM you probably meant to use `HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef`.

**How To Reproduce**

Trying to access `HRTIM1_TIMA` in any code will fail, since `HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef` is undefined:

```c
#include <stm32h7xx.h>
HRTIM1_TIMA->TIMxCR = 0;
```

**Additional context**

```diff
-#define HRTIM1_TIMA         ((HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMA_BASE)
-#define HRTIM1_TIMB         ((HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMB_BASE)
-#define HRTIM1_TIMC         ((HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMC_BASE)
-#define HRTIM1_TIMD         ((HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMD_BASE)
-#define HRTIM1_TIME         ((HRTIM_TIM_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIME_BASE)
+#define HRTIM1_TIMA         ((HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMA_BASE)
+#define HRTIM1_TIMB         ((HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMB_BASE)
+#define HRTIM1_TIMC         ((HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMC_BASE)
+#define HRTIM1_TIMD         ((HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIMD_BASE)
+#define HRTIM1_TIME         ((HRTIM_Timerx_TypeDef *) HRTIM1_TIME_BASE)
```

[Complete patch](https://github.com/modm-io/cmsis-header-stm32/blob/master/patches/h7.patch)
